title: #define AI Engineer - Greg Brockman, OpenAI (ft. Jensen Huang)
talk_summary: A fireside chat with Greg Brockman covering his path to OpenAI, the research/engineering partnership, and how Codex changes software engineering. The most actionable material is about structuring codebases for models (small, well-tested modules), checkpointing long-running agent state, and using a menagerie of models rather than one.

takeaways.technique: Structure codebases for model strengths, not human strengths
takeaways.what_they_do: Break code into small, well-tested modules with fast-running tests, let the model fill in details and run tests itself; keep architecture/connections explicit and simple.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make smaller modules that are well tested that have tests that can be run very quickly um and then fill in the details

takeaways.technique: Tests as the model's feedback loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Because models run tests hundreds/thousands of times more than humans, investing in fast, thorough tests pays off disproportionately; treat it as restoring good engineering practice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model's going to run like these tests like a hundred times or a thousand times more than you will

takeaways.what_they_do: For long-horizon rollouts, snapshot state (including caches) so runs can resume; consider VM-level checkpointing; accept small nondeterministic wiggles on restart.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to start thinking about how to snapshot state and a bunch of things like that

takeaways.technique: Menagerie of models / models using models
takeaways.what_they_do: Expect a diverse set of models with different inference costs and trade-offs; distillation works well; models can call other models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the evidence has really been shifting towards this like menagery of different models

takeaways.what_they_do: Engineers joining a research environment are told to read and listen deeply before changing architecture, because intuitions from web startups often don't transfer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: come in really really listen and kind of assume that that that there's something that you're missing

takeaways.technique: Remove obsolete constraints, not all constraints
takeaways.what_they_do: Map where overhead exists only for constraints that no longer apply, then compress those cycles (e.g., 9-month integration done in 24 hours).
takeaways.evidence_quote: mapping to where is there unnecessary overhead that's there for constraints that are no longer applicable
